text:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has urged youths in Akwa Ibom State to obtain their permanent voter cards (PVCs), describing them as their weapon for determining the country’s political future through the ballot.
Tinubu made the call on Friday in Uyo during a presidential campaign rally, urging young people to collect their PVCs and use them to vote in the next general elections.
“The weapon you have is the PVC. Go ahead and collect your PVCs for the sake of your future. I have promised you a better future, I have promised you development, I have promised you education, I have promised you skill development, I have promised you jobs,” he said.
The president also promised to promote development projects and investments that would create jobs and improve the economic fortunes of Akwa Ibom State.
He specifically highlighted the potential of the state’s agricultural resources, particularly economic trees and palm produce, saying they could support the development of sustainable industries.
“There is no reason why Akwa Ibom cannot use the value of economic trees and palm trees here. There is no reason we cannot create economic skill that is enduring, everlasting,” he said.
Tinubu also approved the upgrade of the existing Victor Attah International Airport to full international status and the proposed Ibom Deep Seaport.
“Now, your leader made a request for international airport status, I approve it,” he said.
On the seaport project, the president said it would bring economic value and promote development in the state.
“Ibom Deep Seaport is approved. Ibom Deep Seaport will bring associated economic value and economic development. We will break the cycle of poverty, ignorance and economic regression. We will make Ibom Seaport possible,” he said.
Also speaking at the rally, Vice President Kashim Shettima and Senate President Godswill Akpabio urged the people of Akwa Ibom to support the All Progressives Congress (APC), saying the Tinubu administration had positively impacted the lives of Nigerians.
Governor Umo Eno pledged to mobilise voters across the state to deliver two million votes for Tinubu’s re-election.
